units.text: What are the requirements of “There is no god but Allah”?
He asks this question and says: What are the requirements of “There is no god but Allah”?

This word is the greatest word. It is the word of Tawhid (monotheism), and a servant does not enter Islam except by realizing it and believing in it, and that there is no true deity except Allah. It is the first word to which the messengers called; the first word to which the messengers call is this word: “There is no god but Allah.” Allah, the Exalted, says: ⟦Q1⟧ [Al-Anbiya: 25] And He, Glorified be He, says: ⟦Q2⟧ [An-Nahl: 36] And when Allah sent our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, the first word to which he called was: “There is no god but Allah,” along with belief in him and that he is the Messenger of Allah. It entails devoting worship sincerely to Allah alone, believing that He is the One truly worthy of worship, that He is the Lord of the worlds, the All-Knowing Creator, and that He alone deserves to be worshipped and His commands obeyed. It also entails that the servant believes that Allah is his Creator, that He has prepared for him Paradise and Hellfire, and that he will inevitably meet his Lord – either Paradise or Hellfire.

This word is the foundation of the religion, the basis of the creed, and the firm handhold. It is essential to believe in it, to hold its meaning with conviction: that there is no true deity except Allah. This belief entails obeying the commands and avoiding the prohibitions – obeying Allah, the Truth, whom you have believed is your true deity. It entails fulfilling His right by worshipping Him through your prayer, fasting, zakah (obligatory almsgiving), Hajj, fasting, and so on. The meaning of “ilah” is the one who is worshipped. The meaning of “There is no god but Allah” is: there is no one truly worthy of worship except Allah.

So it is obligatory upon you to worship Him and devote your prayer, fasting, zakah, Hajj, jihad, and all your acts of worship exclusively to the Lord, Glorified and Exalted be He, worshipping Him alone, hoping for His reward and fearing His punishment, Glorified and Exalted be He.
Likewise, among its requirements is that you believe in what Allah has forbidden for you – shirk (associating partners with Him) and sins – and that you keep away from that and beware of it. Yes.
Presenter: May Allah reward you well.
